query: For high-entropy alloys intended for structural applications, what testable methodological hypothesis could enable improved combinations of strength, ductility, Young’s modulus, and fracture resistance? Explain why it should work, what measurable improvement is expected relative to the state of the art, the conditions under which it should or should not hold, the prior evidence supporting it, and an experimental result that would decisively falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: Controlled precipitation of coherent L12-ordered γ′ nanoprecipitates in an equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi high-entropy alloy matrix—achieved via minor Al and Ti additions followed by cold rolling and low-temperature aging—will simultaneously increase strength, maintain adequate ductility, raise Young’s modulus, and preserve fracture resistance relative to the unmodified alloy.
generation.material_initial_state: Homogeneous, single-phase face-centered cubic CoCrFeMnNi high-entropy alloy.
generation.intervention: Alloying with 3 at.% Al and 3 at.% Ti, 50 % cold rolling thickness reduction, then aging at 400 °C for 24 h.
generation.conditions: Mechanical tests at room temperature (20 °C) and quasi-static strain rate (~10⁻³ s⁻¹). Hypothesis holds for alloys with stacking-fault energy >30 mJ/m² and aging below 500 °C; it is not expected to hold if Al+Ti content <2 at.% or aging temperature ≥500 °C.
generation.structural_mediator: Nanoscale (5–20 nm) coherent L12 γ′ precipitates at ~10–15 vol % within the fcc matrix.
generation.mechanism: Orowan looping and back-stress hardening as mobile dislocations bypass coherent precipitates, combined with modulus mismatch between precipitate and matrix, leading to increased work-hardening rate.
generation.predicted_outcome: Yield strength increases by ≥200 MPa (to >500 MPa), ultimate tensile strength to >900 MPa, Young’s modulus rises by ∼10 % (to >230 GPa), ductility remains ≥40 % elongation, and fracture toughness K_IC stays above 180 MPa√m.
generation.baseline: Equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi: YS ∼300 MPa, UTS ∼700 MPa, elongation ∼60 %, modulus ∼210 GPa, K_IC ∼200 MPa√m.
generation.boundary: Does not apply for Al+Ti additions below 2 at.% or aging at ≥500 °C; excessive cold work (>70 % thickness reduction) may suppress coherent precipitation.
generation.uncertainty: Moderate; precise strength and ductility trade-offs depend sensitively on precipitate size distribution and matrix composition.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare three alloys: (1) base CoCrFeMnNi, (2) CoCrFeMnNi+3 at.% Al+3 at.% Ti without aging, and (3) CoCrFeMnNi+3 at.% Al+3 at.% Ti with 50 % cold rolling and 400 °C/24 h aging. Characterize precipitate size and volume fraction by TEM. Perform tensile tests (measure YS, UTS, elongation), resonance ultrasound for modulus, and compact-tension tests for K_IC.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the aged, Al+Ti-doped alloy fails to show ≥150 MPa increase in yield strength or fails to form ≥8 vol % coherent γ′ precipitates, or if similar strengthening occurs in the unaged or base alloys, then the hypothesis is falsified.
